newsitem.title: CHINA: Shanghai soybean futures end down in slow trade.
newsitem.headline: Shanghai soybean futures end down in slow trade.

text.p: Shanghai soybean futures ended mostly down in slow trade on Monday on speculative selling, traders said.
The most actively traded January 1998 contract ended at an intraday low of 3,340 yuan ($403) per tonne, losing 10 yuan. It opened at 3,360 and hit a high of 3,364 yuan per tonne.
July was unchanged at 3,250 yuan per tonne, September fell seven to 3,288, November rose 20 to 3,298 and the March 1998 contract dropped three to 3,365 yuan per tonne.
Combined volume fell to 16,600 tonnes from 17,400 tonnes.
Soybeans opened mostly lower and moved at low levels for most of the session, traders said.
"Speculative players dominated today's trading with some capital seen coming from the domestic stock market now that the government is trying to cool things down," one trader said.

Beijing last week announced it would ban state enterprises and listed firms from speculative stock trading, in a move aimed at curbing the inflow of "hot money" into the country's overheating stock market.
Traders said they expected soybeans to move around current levels in the next few days. ($1=8.2930 yuan)
